title: Plasma shell terminated by kernel for memory usage when deleting a .ics calendar from KOrganizer
line: Deleting a calendar shown in the clock's PIM events no longer freezes Plasma and fills memory until it is killed.
explanation: When a calendar is deleted, the PIM events plugin reports every one of its events as removed, one after another. DaysModel::onEventRemoved reset the whole model for each of them, even for events not shown, so the month view recreated all of its day delegates dozens of times without returning to the event loop; plasmashell froze and its memory grew by ~200 MB/s until the OOM killer stepped in. The change (open MR !7183, applied unchanged) queues removed uids and applies them with a single reset on the next event-loop pass, skipping the reset when nothing shown is affected, and flushes pending removals before new or modified data so remove-then-re-add stays in order.

commits.message:
components/calendar: Batch event removals in DaysModel

DaysModel reset itself once per removed event, so deleting a calendar
made the month view rebuild every delegate for each of its events until
plasmashell ran out of memory. Removals are now applied in one batch.

BUG: 492334

media.caption: Master: after the calendar (reporter's .ics, 62 events) is deleted, plasmashell grows ~200 MB/s and is killed at the 3 GB cap after 13 s
With the fix: memory stays flat at ~400 MB; all 62 removals are handled at once
Master: the clock popup was open when the calendar was deleted; plasmashell was killed and restarted, popup gone
With the fix: the popup stays open and the deleted calendar's event dots disappear right away

review.text: Solid fix (from open MR !7183) that batches DaysModel::onEventRemoved calls into a single queued processPendingRemovals() pass, skips resetting the model when no displayed dates are affected, flushes pending removals before onDataReady/onEventModified to preserve remove-then-re-add ordering, and moves agendaUpdated emissions outside beginResetModel()/endResetModel(). Memory profiling and UI screenshots clearly verify that deleting a large calendar no longer freezes or OOMs plasmashell.
